what_it_does: PIM (Processing In Memory) accelerators place compute units inside DRAM chips to avoid the slow data movement between main memory and processors. Modern DRAM PIM designs use bank-level SIMD (single instruction, multiple data) parallelism, where all memory banks must activate in lockstep before any computation begins. This synchronization requirement is expensive: the time to activate rows in memory exceeds the actual computation time, limiting speed. Simply removing synchronization (running asynchronously) saves activation overhead but requires large shared accumulators per bank, wasting area. SplitSync proposes a hybrid approach: each bank group (a cluster of banks) operates asynchronously to hide activation overhead, but within each bank group the banks operate synchronously so no shared accumulators are needed. This balances the tradeoff between hiding latency and minimizing area waste.
